title: A Safehouse for the Debt
premise: Ulyana Oyelaran, an insomniac private security contractor haunted by a client death she can't fully remember, is approached by a stranger named Tomas who insists she once saved his life — a favor she has no memory of. He repays it by warning her that a coordinated attack is scheduled to destroy the safehouse network she helps run, staged to look like a gas accident, and that her own firm may be complicit. As Ulyana investigates, fragmented memories surface suggesting she witnessed more of 'the incident' than she admitted, and that Tomas's debt is a lever someone else is pulling through him. In the end, Ulyana exposes the inside man, stops the attack at the cost of burning her career, and finally sleeps — choosing to build a new kind of safehouse for people like herself.
about_author: Mara Delacroix is the pen name of a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments before turning to fiction. She lives in Lisbon, where she writes thrillers about people who protect strangers for a living.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. On four hours' sleep, she runs a routine protection detail in Lagos, flinching at a car backfire that isn't a shot. A stranger, Tomas, corners her afterward claiming she saved his life two years ago. She remembers nothing. Beat: unease planted beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Tomas leaves a burner phone and a warning: an attack on the Meridian safehouse network, disguised as a gas explosion, weeks away. Ulyana checks his story and finds one true detail she never told anyone. Beat: reluctant curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Clients Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She briefs her boss, Adeyemi, who dismisses the warning but quietly reassigns her away from Meridian — which feels less like caution than containment. Flashback fragments of 'the incident' intrude. Beat: first suspicion that her own house is rotten.

chapters.title: The Incident, Partially Remembered
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, intercut with a memory. Insomnia drives her through old case files; she reconstructs the night a client died in her care and notices a gap — forty minutes missing from her own account. Beat: self-doubt weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Tomas's Ledger
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. We learn why he believes he owes Ulyana: she pulled him from a burning vehicle, though records show no rescue occurred. He's being coached by an anonymous handler feeding him the attack details. Beat: sympathy for a man who may be a pawn.

chapters.title: Gas Lines and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She inspects the Meridian building under pretext and finds the utility schematics have been altered — recently, and with internal access codes. Beat: the threat becomes physical, architectural.

chapters.title: The Inside Man's Shadow
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Someone searches her apartment while she's out; nothing stolen, only her incident files disturbed. She realizes whoever altered the schematics knows she's looking. Beat: hunted without proof.

chapters.title: A Debt With Two Signatures
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. His handler pushes him to lure Ulyana to a dead drop; instead he warns her off, torn between gratitude and coercion. Ulyana catches the drop anyway and photographs the exchange. Beat: alliance forming across mistrust.

chapters.title: Meridian's Quiet Partners
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Following the money, she finds Meridian's insurance was doubled six weeks ago — someone expects the building to burn. Adeyemi's name appears adjacent, not guilty, but close. Beat: betrayal at the institutional level.

chapters.title: Forty Missing Minutes
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, deep flashback. The full incident resurfaces: her client wasn't killed by chance — he was silenced, and Ulyana saw the man who did it. She reported it; the report vanished. Beat: memory restored, identity shaken.

chapters.title: The Man From the Fire
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The face from her recovered memory matches a current Meridian contractor: Viktor Reiss, safety officer, author of the altered gas schematics. Beat: the past and present attacks are the same hand.

chapters.title: Counter-Surveillance
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Reiss's people tail Tomas; he burns his own cover to shake them, calling Ulyana from a rooftop as they close in. She extracts him through the city's night markets. Beat: trust earned in motion.

chapters.title: What Adeyemi Knew
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Confronting her boss, she learns he buried her original report under pressure from above — not malice, fear. He gives her a name: the client who ordered the silencing now sits on Meridian's board. Beat: the conspiracy gets a face.

chapters.title: The Board Member's Evening
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She infiltrates a board dinner as catering security, copying Reiss's schedule from a shared tablet. The attack date surfaces: eleven days out, during a full-building evacuation drill — perfect cover. Beat: clock starts ticking loudly.

chapters.title: Drill Schedule, Real Casualties
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Reiss tests the gas delivery system early using an abandoned wing; a homeless man dies of 'carbon monoxide poisoning.' Tomas realizes the plan is live, not theoretical. Beat: stakes turn mortal.

chapters.title: Burning the Whistle
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She sends evidence to regulators; within hours her credentials are revoked and a warrant names her for the original client's death — the frame completed. Beat: everything taken, resolve hardened.

chapters.title: The Safehouse Underground
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Tomas's alternating POV. Fugitives now, they shelter in a decommissioned Meridian sub-basement safehouse only Ulyana knows, planning to trigger the evacuation themselves and catch Reiss mid-attack. Beat: dark-night resolve, partnership sealed.

chapters.title: Eleven Days Become One
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Reiss moves the date up after spotting their surveillance; the attack is tomorrow. They scramble to pre-position shutoffs and alert the tenants Reiss trusts least. Beat: compressed, breathless preparation.

chapters.title: The Night of the Accident
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Gas begins flowing during the 'drill'; Ulyana reaches the main valve as Reiss seals the control room. Tomas draws security away at gunpoint he hopes he'll never use. Beat: climax ignition.

chapters.title: What the Fire Didn't Take
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She forces the valve shut, fights Reiss in the flooding dark, and chooses arrest over killing him — recording his confession as sirens arrive. Beat: victory purchased with restraint.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Weeks later, her recovered memory and recordings clear her name and gut the board; Adeyemi testifies, Tomas disappears owing nothing. Ulyana declines rehiring. Beat: justice without restoration — yet.

chapters.title: A Safehouse for the Debt
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She opens a small refuge for witnesses and burned-out protectors, staffed by people who owe each other favors that did happen. That night, she sleeps through until morning. Beat: belonging found; themes resolved.
